Official Mumbai Dataflow rates used for planning: $0.0759/vCPU-hour, $0.0042684/GiB-hour memory, and $0.0000648/GiB-hour standard persistent disk. For 2 vCPU + 7.5 GiB + 30 GiB over 15 minutes: ($0.183813 compute/hour + $0.001944 disk/hour) × 0.25 = $0.04643925 (₹4.64 at an explicit planning conversion of ₹100/USD). Streaming Engine is pinned off; the source-to-sink template has no explicit shuffle transform. Add a conservative 100 MiB Logging reserve at $0.50/GiB ($4.88), 100 MiB of staging objects retained for seven days at a deliberately high $0.05/GiB-month assumption (about ₹0.12), and ₹1 for Pub/Sub, one small BigQuery streaming row, and up to 1,000 standard-class Cloud Storage operations. Modeled 15-minute total is about ₹10.65; 30 minutes under the same assumptions is about ₹15.29. These are conditional estimates, not quotes or caps; actual project free-tier consumption, log volume, object activity and runtime are unknown. No enforced shutdown/billing cap exists; Dataflow may continue billing after a drain request until it reaches DRAINED.

The Playbook estimates 3–5 minute startup. Proposed operation is one <=1 KiB message, observe delivery, then drain immediately; initiate drain no later than 10 minutes after launch if delivery is not confirmed, and verify no active jobs after DRAINED. The 15-minute/₹15 limit cannot be guaranteed if startup, drain, API access or job termination overruns the manual window.
After a future authorized drain, rerun the active-job listing command and confirm it returns no active jobs.
Streaming jobs may incur ongoing charges.
